translation.english_text: [Before Manoharan.]
Aha! After offering a sacrifice like this, for Vasanthan's coronation to take place is, according to shastra, a most excellent thing!
notes: `சாஸ்திரப்படி` is retained as `according to shastra` rather than secularized.

translation.english_text: Yes. The opportunity has fallen into our hands by itself. Vasanthan is fortunate.

The young breeze of the Chola Empire—poor tender infant. For the sins of the father, this bud is going to die. Manohara! Look once upon the beautiful face of your child. Gather upon your lips all the longing you have held down, and give your child's tender cheek one last kiss.

[He stretches the child toward Manoharan, taunting him.]

Come—bathe your child, your fruit of nectar, in your tears!
notes: The bud, young-breeze and tear-bath images are retained.
The source-unlabelled continuation and intervening child-taunt action remain inside the preceding explicit Ugrasenan record.

source_locator.description: Manoharan is shaken; the child smiles without understanding.

translation.english_text: [Manoharan is shaken; the child, knowing nothing, smiles.]

Hmm, you are smiling—poor thing, smile well. Born crying, you will die smiling. Is it not Pandya blood and Chola blood that run surging through your body? Perhaps that is why, with such joy, you will sleep in the cradle of death.
Quickly! [Ugrasenan raises his sword over the child.]
notes: Source-attached action remains within the labelled turn.

translation.english_text: Sena! [She runs in screaming.] Cast the killing sword upon me first.

That cannot be! You must feast your eyes on this child falling into the cruel mouth of the goddess of death. Only after that shall I watch in ecstasy as the Chola line bursts into a hundred pieces and scatters into dust.

Stop, Vasanthi, stop! For many years you made my husband yours and turned my life into a moonless sky. I endured it. You sat beside the emperor in the assembly hall like the great empress of the empire. I endured that too. With wicked words you killed me without killing me; even that I endured. Whenever my son rose roaring like a tiger, I stopped at once the sword springing from its sheath and saved your life. Why? You witless woman who holds the golden idol of the Chola land at knife-point—I ask you: why was I patient?
notes: The repeated `I endured` structure, moonless-sky image and unsheathed-sword image are preserved.
Physical source word split PDF 83→84 is represented in English page segments.

red it. You sat beside the emperor in the assembly hall like the great empress of the empire. I endured that too. With wicked words you killed me without killing me; even that I endured. Whenever my son rose roaring like a tiger, I stopped at once the sword springing from its sheath and saved your life. Why? You witless woman who holds the golden idol of the Chola land at knife-point—I ask you: why was I patient?

translation.english_text: That is the karma of your former birth.
notes: `பூர்வ ஜன்ம வினை` is translated in its source religious register.

translation.english_text: No—love for my husband. You belonged to him. I thought I must not harm what was his and bring grief to my husband. But today you have imprisoned my husband himself. Vasantha Sena, in the name of the patience I have shown until this day, I ask you. It is the country you want, is it not? Take it. Rule your kingdom! The forest is enough for us. Let all of us go.
Ah! Let you go? Do not dream! In another half a moment, the ash-heap of the Chola Empire will be piled at my feet.
Vasantha Sena! If the very form of truth rises as a storm, you will sink into that ash-heap. Beware!
You dare threaten me?

Yes—you. A land where the sky pours rain! A forest where deer roam! A home where honey showers—our Chola realm. You came there bearing the kamandalam of love, devised plot after plot and plundered a beautiful life. I welcomed the woman who came and gave her space to live in pleasure all these days! And today you speak with arrogance: you to rule, we to perish. No! You yourself are performing the aarti for your own destruction. Do not perish in vain!
notes: The land/forest/home parallelism, `love-kamandalam`, rule/perish antithesis and self-aarti image are preserved.
Physical source split across PDF 84→85 is retained in page segments.

You came there bearing the kamandalam of love, devised plot after plot and plundered a beautiful life. I welcomed the woman who came and gave her space to live in pleasure all these days! And today you speak with arro—
gance: you to rule, we to perish. No! You yourself are performing the aarti for your own destruction. Do not perish in vain!

translation.english_text: What did you say?
[Vasanthi slaps Padmavathi.]
Mother!...... [He cries out.]
Manohara! [She goes to him.]

Manohara! My unfading lamp of fame! Forgive me, da! Whenever you rose in valour to compose a heroic epic in defence of the greatness of the Chola Empire, it was I—the culprit—who hid the stylus, concealed the palm leaves and stood in your way. My gold, who bore your mother's command upon your head! Even if your own mother now commands you, ‘Destroy injustice,’ you have been brought to a state where you cannot move, my treasure! Ruined. Everything is ruined.
notes: The heroic-epic/stylus/palm-leaf image and repeated maternal address are retained.

translation.english_text: No, Mother......! No! My own mother—now give the order, the command: ‘Destroy injustice!’ The final hour! The final plea! My Tamil Mother! After seeing this outrage—the little jackal that entered this land through a pass opening amid the pleasure-grove, settled here, and today has laid the first token for climbing the throne—will you at least now grant permission? I need no sword, Mother! One spoken word is enough. I need no army, Mother—only let the mother's ban be lifted! Give me no blade, Mother—one glance of the eye is enough—and freedom for you, for me, for everyone. Where is the order, Mother? Give the order. I shall erase these people until no trace of their form remains.
notes: `தமிழ்த் தாயே` remains `Tamil Mother`; the jackal/pass/throne imagery and sword/word, army/ban, blade/glance parallelism are preserved.

translation.english_text: My precious treasure! It was for your father's good that I bound your heroic hands. I bowed my head before this venomous woman. After the very man for whose sake I kept saying patience, patience has himself been locked in prison, where is the greatness left in patience? Manohara! Enough endurance. Rise in a surge!
notes: The `பொறுமை / பெருமை` patience/greatness turn and `பொங்கியெழு` eruptive command are preserved.
Physical source break PDF 85→86 is retained.

english_page_segments.english_text: My precious treasure! It was for your father's good that I bound your heroic hands.

I bowed my head before this venomous woman. After the very man for whose sake I kept saying patience, patience has himself been locked in prison, where is the greatness left in patience? Manohara! Enough endurance. Rise in a surge!

translation.english_text: Mother!
The mother's command has been given. Set forth! Manohara! Manohara!! Manohara!! Manohara!!!
notes: The escalating repetitions and punctuation are retained.

source_locator.description: Padmavathi runs to the king's statue.

translation.english_text: [She runs to the king's statue.]
Maharaja! Do you see how our treasured family is being destroyed? Look at Manoharan, bound and writhing. Look at Manoharan, Maharaja! Maharaja!! Maharaja!!!
[Ugrasenan and Vasanthi laugh.]

Why are you laughing? Monkeys leaping in a red-banana grove! Great sinners who came to bend this land, one in the form of a woman, one in the form of a holy man! You who forgot the history the world tells—that those who laughed so have not lived, and those who wept have not been ruined! Little pack of jackals who came by sleight of hand to break the sceptre of the flourishing Tamils! Do not laugh! Pack of villains unable to know the power of tears! Do not laugh, forgetting that tears have accomplished what even the point of a sword has not. Traitors who, amid the afflicted, compose sandhu and sing sindhu—do not laugh, do not laugh...... O soil of the motherland! Look at Manoharan, the sacred lamp of your house! Chola Mother! Look at the agony of the warrior of warriors who placed a victory-garland upon your beautiful shoulder. Look at the son who marked your lovely forehead with tilak from the blood of foreign enemies—alas!—now bound and suffering in the fetters of slavery. O ceremonial hall of the Chola family, how long will you make the form of my victory bow his head amid these useless men? A tender infant—the crown prince! A king who is to rule. O Mother Earth who bears the sinner thirsting to avenge herself upon them all! If it is true that you are grateful; if it is true that the tears of mothers born in the warrior clan possess power; if it is true that the great warrior Manoharan, who has never known how to kneel before an outsider, is my son—let these chains shatter into fragments, let the laughter of the unjust cease, let this very hall collapse into dust. Into dust! Into dust!! Into dust!!!
notes: The speech is preserved in full: red-banana monkeys, woman/holy-man disguises, tears-versus-sword, motherland/Chola Mother, victory-garland, blood-tilak, slavery-fetters and the final threefold dust invocation all remain visible.
`சந்து புனை சிந்து பாடும்` is retained conservatively as `compose sandhu and sing sindhu` rather than replaced by an unsupported literary interpretation.
Physical PDF 86→87 boundary remains explicit.

source_locator.description: Manoharan breaks the pillar, aided by the mother's voice.

translation.english_text: [By Manoharan's strength the pillar breaks and falls; the voice of motherhood too becomes his aid.]
Seize him! Arrest him!
Stab him! Kill him.

source_locator.description: Ugrasenan is killed; Pandya forces arrive; Kesari Varman saves the child.

translation.english_text: [Ugrasenan is killed by Manoharan; the Pandya army also arrives. Kesari Varman saves the child.]

source_locator.description: Vasanthi's dagger meant for Manoharan strikes Vasanthan.

translation.english_text: [The dagger Vasanthi throws at Manoharan strikes Vasanthan.]
Vasantha!
Anna!
Vasantha...! Vasantha...! Vasantha...!
Anna!
Anna, will you not call me ‘thambi’ just once! Say it, Anna—say ‘thambi’!
notes: `தம்பி` is retained as `thambi` because the kinship word itself is the emotional point of the exchange.

translation.english_text: Thambi!
notes: `தம்பி` is retained as `thambi` because the kinship word itself is the emotional point of the exchange.

translation.english_text: Anna! If the dagger this sinner threw had struck you, I understand how much pain you would suffer. You must live, Anna! Anna, you must rule the country! I must die.

source_locator.description: Vasanthan dies; Manoharan moves to kill Vasanthi.

translation.english_text: [Vasanthan dies. As Manoharan tries to kill Vasanthi...]
No, Prince! Leave her to me. I have waited many days for this good deed. She must not die in a single stroke. Until her final breath, she must be killed little... by little. [Vasanthi runs.]
notes: The source's deliberately cruel `little... by little` rhythm is preserved; the translation does not soften it.

translation.english_text: Where are you running? Woman born to rule! Unruly shrew—stop! Stop!
[The prison door opens.]
Satyaseelar! Forgive me. Where is Padmavathi? Where is my Padmavathi!
Come with me.
Rajapriya! Rajam priya!
notes: The compact source word-play `ராஜப் பிரியா! ராஜம் பிரியா!` is retained transliteratively rather than forcing an uncertain paraphrase.
